note: Open*Hubs BACKEND POWERING — CANDIDATE registry. Catalogs the open-source repos that could power the backend COMPONENTS of the original tracked backend candidate hubs (OpenContextHub, OpenSkillsHub, OpenToolsHub, OpenMCPHub, OpenCompressionHub, OpenBenchmarkHub, OpenHubForAI). The design family has since expanded to 21 Open*Hubs; add backend candidate records for newer hubs before claiming backend coverage for them. GOVERNANCE LAW: discovery != trust; candidate != active; benchmark result = EVIDENCE, never promotion authority; output != truth; the Open*Hubs are REGISTRIES, NOT truth authorities (Baltor governs truth, Teleon runs capabilities). Every external repo here is a CANDIDATE behind a port with a local_equivalent + license + proof_to_promote, and is NEVER auto-active. This registry triggers NO install, NO live run, NO Docker, NO network call, NO API key, NO dataset push; it is metadata only. Strongest insight: OpenMCPHub can WRAP/FORK the open-source OFFICIAL MCP registry (modelcontextprotocol/registry), which is explicitly designed so anyone can build a compatible sub-registry.

governance_law.discovery_neq_trust: appearing in a discovery aggregator (Glama/Smithery/mcp.so) or scoring high there is discovery signal, never trust; an item must clear governance before it powers a hub backend.
governance_law.candidate_neq_active: cataloged behind a port with a local_equivalent != wired into a live hub backend; promotion to active requires the proof_to_promote ladder + owner authorization (esp. for Docker/network/cloud).
governance_law.benchmark_eq_evidence: a benchmark/eval result is EVIDENCE for a scorecard; it can never by itself promote a candidate to active.
governance_law.output_neq_truth: LLM/agent/eval output is never truth; the Open*Hubs are REGISTRIES (metadata/index surfaces), NOT truth authorities — only Baltor governs truth.
governance_law.local_first: every gated (Docker/network) candidate must have a local_equivalent so a hub backend has an offline golden path before any external dependency is wired.

status_codes.candidate: cataloged; wrapped behind a port; local_equivalent first; promotes to active only after proof_to_promote + owner authorization
status_codes.reference: external yardstick/standard we point at; not run in this repo
status_codes.active: FORBIDDEN for an external Open*Hub backend repo without proof — promotion requires owner approval + the full proof_to_promote ladder + a local_equivalent

cross_references.agent_environment_research_registry.json: Repo2RLEnv / Harbor / OpenEnv (benchmark/harness environments) are cataloged THERE; NOT duplicated here — cross-ref for OpenBenchmarkHub/OpenHubForAI environment backends.
cross_references.open_hubs_bridge_graph.json: canonical hub relationship chain + the 'hubs are not truth authorities' law.

entries.name: Official MCP Registry (modelcontextprotocol/registry)
entries.local_equivalent: run the Go registry service locally against a local Postgres (or its in-memory/SQLite dev store); serve seed MCP server metadata from a local fixture — no public network needed for the golden path.
entries.proof_to_promote: fork/wrap behind an McpRegistryProviderPort; local seed-data offline run; license/provenance proof; sub-registry namespacing proof (OpenMCPHub namespace != upstream); no-auto-trust gate (listed server = candidate, never active); owner authorizes any public-network sync.
entries.note: STRONGEST backend candidate for any hub: the official registry is OPEN SOURCE and EXPLICITLY designed so anyone can build a COMPATIBLE SUB-REGISTRY — OpenMCPHub forks/wraps it rather than reinventing a registry service. Reference implementation of the generic registry_service pattern (metadata pointing at npm/PyPI/Docker packages).

entries.name: Glama MCP server directory
entries.local_equivalent: ingest a cached/exported snapshot of discovery metadata into the local registry; the public crawl is an enrichment, not the golden path.
entries.proof_to_promote: snapshot-ingest behind a DiscoveryFeedPort; discovery != trust gate (scored/listed != promoted); license/ToS check on redistribution; owner authorizes the live crawl.
entries.note: Discovery aggregator (10k+ servers, scored). Score/listing is DISCOVERY signal, NOT trust — every discovered server enters OpenMCPHub as a candidate.

entries.name: Smithery MCP registry
entries.local_equivalent: cached snapshot ingest behind the DiscoveryFeedPort, same as Glama.
entries.proof_to_promote: snapshot-ingest behind DiscoveryFeedPort; discovery != trust gate; ToS/license check; owner authorizes live crawl.
entries.note: Discovery aggregator (7k+ servers). Enrichment feed only; not a truth authority.

entries.name: mcp.so directory
entries.local_equivalent: cached snapshot ingest behind the DiscoveryFeedPort.
entries.proof_to_promote: snapshot-ingest behind DiscoveryFeedPort; discovery != trust gate; ToS/license check; owner authorizes live crawl.
entries.note: Largest discovery directory (~20k listings). Breadth signal; every listing is a candidate, never auto-active.

entries.name: microsoft/mcp-gateway
entries.local_equivalent: a thin in-process reverse-proxy stub honoring the same routing contract, no K8s — exercises the OpenMCPHub serving surface offline.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind an McpGatewayPort; local in-process stub; sandbox proof; owner authorizes Docker/K8s; license verification.
entries.note: Kubernetes reverse-proxy gateway for MCP. Optional serving layer; CONTAINER/K8s-gated, so owner-gated and candidate-only.

entries.name: Docker MCP Gateway
entries.local_equivalent: in-process gateway stub (no Docker) honoring the gateway contract for the offline golden path.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind McpGatewayPort; local stub; container-isolation proof; owner authorizes Docker; license verification.
entries.note: Container-native MCP gateway. CONTAINER-gated — explicitly owner-gated per repo guardrails; candidate only.

entries.name: IBM ContextForge (MCP Gateway)
entries.local_equivalent: in-process federation stub honoring the gateway/federation contract, offline.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind McpGatewayPort; local stub; sandbox/isolation proof; owner authorizes Docker; license verification.
entries.note: Gateway + federation + admin layer for MCP. Optional serving/federation layer; container-gated; candidate only.

entries.name: pgvector
entries.local_equivalent: local Postgres + pgvector extension (the repo's existing pgvector load path); no external service needed.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind a VectorSearchPort; local Postgres golden path; dimension/config from a single source of truth; license verification (PostgreSQL license is permissive — confirm).
entries.note: SIMPLEST vector backend for OpenContextHub — a Postgres extension, no new datastore. Recommended default; aligns with the repo's existing pgvector plans.

entries.name: Qdrant
entries.local_equivalent: embedded/local single-node Qdrant or the pgvector golden path as the offline fallback behind the same VectorSearchPort.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind VectorSearchPort; local single-node proof; owner authorizes Docker; license verification.
entries.note: Rust vector DB; strong scale/filtering. Container-typical deployment → candidate; pgvector is the lower-friction default.

entries.name: Weaviate
entries.local_equivalent: local single-node Weaviate or a Postgres FTS + pgvector hybrid stub behind a HybridSearchPort for the offline path.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind HybridSearchPort; local stub; owner authorizes Docker; license verification.
entries.note: Native hybrid search with relativeScoreFusion (vector + keyword). Container-gated; candidate.

entries.name: LanceDB
entries.local_equivalent: embedded in-process LanceDB on the local filesystem — already an embedded library, no service.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind VectorSearchPort; in-process local proof; license verification.
entries.note: EMBEDDED in-process vector store (no server). Excellent local-first / offline-golden-path option for OpenContextHub alongside pgvector.

entries.name: Milvus
entries.local_equivalent: Milvus Lite (embedded) or the pgvector golden path behind the VectorSearchPort.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind VectorSearchPort; Milvus-Lite/pgvector local proof; owner authorizes Docker for full Milvus; license verification.
entries.note: Large-scale distributed vector DB. Heavy for a public read surface; candidate for high-scale tier only.

entries.name: OpenSearch
entries.local_equivalent: Postgres FTS + pgvector hybrid stub behind the HybridSearchPort for offline; OpenSearch is the scale tier.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind HybridSearchPort; local stub; owner authorizes Docker/JVM; license verification.
entries.note: Lucene-based search + k-NN vector plugin (hybrid). Heavy JVM/container footprint; candidate for scale.

entries.name: Meilisearch
entries.local_equivalent: run the single Meilisearch binary locally on the filesystem (no Docker required) for the public read-surface search; offline-capable.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind a KeywordSearchPort; local-binary proof; license verification (MIT).
entries.note: Fast keyword/typo-tolerant search for the public READ surface of any hub. Single binary — light to run locally. Recommended search layer for the static-site front of the hubs.

entries.name: Typesense
entries.local_equivalent: local Typesense binary, or Meilisearch as the non-copyleft alternative behind the same KeywordSearchPort.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind KeywordSearchPort; local-binary proof; LICENSE REVIEW REQUIRED (GPL-3.0 copyleft implications for distribution) before any promotion.
entries.note: Fast search engine (instant-search). CAVEAT: GPL-3.0 — copyleft; license review required before backend adoption. Meilisearch (MIT) is the lower-risk default.

entries.name: Inspect AI (UK AISI)
entries.local_equivalent: run Inspect tasks against a local/mock model provider; task + tool-use definitions execute offline with stubbed solvers — model calls are the only network need and can be mocked.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind an EvalHarnessPort; local/mock-model task proof; secret-hygiene (env:// refs only); EvalRunReceipt; benchmark=evidence gate; license verification (MIT).
entries.note: RECOMMENDED eval harness for OpenHubForAI: task + tool-use native, framework-grade, MIT, from UK AISI. Eval result is EVIDENCE for a scorecard, never promotion authority.

entries.name: lm-evaluation-harness (EleutherAI)
entries.local_equivalent: run a single task against a local/mock model; the academic benchmark suites are the reference yardstick we compare against, not live infra.
entries.proof_to_promote: if ever wrapped: behind a BenchmarkRunnerPort; local/mock-model proof; secret-hygiene; benchmark=evidence gate; license verification (MIT).
entries.note: De-facto academic base-model benchmark runner — REFERENCE yardstick for OpenBenchmarkHub. A score here is evidence, never a promotion authority.

entries.name: promptfoo
entries.local_equivalent: YAML eval configs run against a local/mock provider; assertions execute offline.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind EvalHarnessPort; local/mock-model proof; secret-hygiene; benchmark=evidence gate; license verification; RE-VERIFY governance/ownership given the OpenAI acquisition.
entries.note: YAML-driven eval + red-team harness. CAVEAT: reportedly acquired into OpenAI (Mar 2026) — re-verify project governance/independence before any backend reliance; treat as candidate, watch for license/control changes.

entries.name: DeepEval
entries.local_equivalent: pytest-native metrics run locally; LLM-as-judge metrics can target a local/mock model.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind EvalHarnessPort; local/mock-model proof; secret-hygiene; benchmark=evidence gate; license verification.
entries.note: Pytest-native eval with agent/RAG metrics. Some metrics use LLM-as-judge → output != truth (judge output is evidence, not ground truth).

entries.name: Ragas
entries.local_equivalent: RAG metrics computed locally against fixture contexts; judge model can be local/mock.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind EvalHarnessPort; local fixture proof; secret-hygiene; benchmark=evidence gate; license verification.
entries.note: RAG-specific eval metrics (faithfulness, context precision/recall). Pairs with OpenContextHub for context-quality evidence; judge output is evidence, not truth.

entries.name: Microsoft LLMLingua
entries.local_equivalent: runs locally with a small local compressor model on CPU/GPU; no hosted API required for the golden path.
entries.proof_to_promote: wrap behind a ContextCompressionPort; LOSSLESS-distillation proof (raw context + lineage preserved, answer-critical facts + source handles survive, rehydration provable); local-model proof; license verification (MIT).
entries.note: RECOMMENDED compression backend for OpenCompressionHub (LLMLingua + LLMLingua-2; up to ~20x, 4-10x in production). MUST honor the repo's Lossless Distillation law — compression shrinks the text surface only if answer-critical facts + source handles survive; the original context is preserved.

entries.name: SKILL.md open format (agentskills spec)
entries.local_equivalent: parse/validate SKILL.md files locally against the open format spec; the format is a standard we conform to, no service needed.
entries.proof_to_promote: if a registry is built on it: SkillRegistryPort + local validation + a skill-content SECURITY SCAN gate (see vuln caveat) + provenance/signed-publisher + license verification of the spec.
entries.note: Open skill format (originally Anthropic, now an open standard). REFERENCE format OpenSkillsHub conforms to. CAVEAT: ~13%+ of marketplace skills reportedly carry critical vulns → a security/scan gate is mandatory; a listed skill is a candidate, never auto-active.

entries.name: OpenSkillsHub registry service (MCP-registry pattern)
entries.local_equivalent: fork the MCP registry service pattern locally over local Postgres, storing SkillArtifact metadata that points at skill packages; offline golden path.
entries.proof_to_promote: fork/wrap behind a SkillRegistryPort; local seed-data offline run; skill-content security-scan gate; provenance/license; sub-registry namespacing; no-auto-trust gate.
entries.note: Reuses the OSS MCP registry as the generic registry_service pattern for SkillArtifacts (metadata -> package pointers). Same wrap-the-reference-implementation play as OpenMCPHub.

entries.name: OpenToolsHub registry service (MCP-registry pattern)
entries.local_equivalent: fork the MCP registry service pattern locally over local Postgres for ToolArtifact metadata; tool/MCP-tool discovery overlaps OpenMCPHub's Glama/Smithery/mcp.so feeds (snapshot-ingested, not live).
entries.proof_to_promote: fork/wrap behind a ToolRegistryPort; local seed-data offline run; discovery != trust gate on ingested catalogs; provenance/license; no-auto-trust gate.
entries.note: OpenToolsHub's tool catalog overlaps OpenMCPHub discovery sources (MCP tools). Reuses the OSS MCP registry pattern; discovered tools are candidates, never auto-active.

entries.name: OpenBenchmarkHub registry service (MCP-registry pattern)
entries.local_equivalent: fork the MCP registry service pattern locally over local Postgres for BenchmarkArtifact metadata; benchmark RUNNERS (lm-eval-harness, Inspect) and environments (Repo2RLEnv/Harbor, cataloged in agent_environment_research_registry.json) are referenced, not embedded.
entries.proof_to_promote: fork/wrap behind a BenchmarkRegistryPort; local seed-data offline run; benchmark=evidence gate (a stored result never promotes anything); provenance/license; no-auto-trust gate.
entries.note: OpenBenchmarkHub = registry of benchmarks + pointers to runners/environments. Cross-ref agent_environment_research_registry.json for the environment backends (do not duplicate). A benchmark result is EVIDENCE, never promotion authority.
